title: What is the baptism “for the dead” of 1 Corinthians 15:29?
summary: 1 Corinthians 15:29 asks “what shall they do which are baptized for the dead, if the dead rise not at all? why are they then baptized for the dead?” The verse does not say who “they” are, what baptism “for the dead” consisted of, or whether Paul approves of it.
text: KJV 1 Corinthians 15:29: “what shall they do which are baptized for the dead, if the dead rise not at all? why are they then baptized for the dead?”. Greek New Testament (Tischendorf, eighth edition) 1 Corinthians 15:29: οἱ βαπτιζόμενοι ὑπὲρ τῶν νεκρῶν [those being baptized for the dead]. KJV 1 Corinthians 15:30: “why stand we in jeopardy every hour”. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/46/15/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/46/15/.
reasoning: The verse uses a third person plural (“they”) and does not say whose practice it names, whether those baptized were living believers acting for dead people, or whether “for the dead” has another sense (for the sake of the hope of the dead, or on behalf of the dead in Christ). It uses the practice as part of an argument from the resurrection and does not say whether Paul approves or only points to what they do. Different readings are held as possibilities only; the text does not choose among them.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. The question is limited to 1 Corinthians 15:29 and its argument in 15:12–34. The record does not say which reading is right and does not claim that no other passage of the Bible says more. title: What was Paul’s “thorn in the flesh” (2 Corinthians 12:7)?
summary: 2 Corinthians 12:7 says that “there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me”. The verse does not say what the thorn was, and 12:8–9 say only that Paul asked three times that it depart and was told “My grace is sufficient for thee”.
text: KJV 2 Corinthians 12:7: “there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me”. Greek New Testament (Tischendorf, eighth edition) 2 Corinthians 12:7: ἐδόθη μοι σκόλοψ τῇ σαρκί [there was given to me a stake in the flesh]. KJV 2 Corinthians 12:8: “I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me”. KJV 2 Corinthians 12:9: “My grace is sufficient for thee”. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/47/12/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/47/12/.
reasoning: The verse names the thing by a figure (a thorn, or stake, “in the flesh”) and calls it a “messenger of Satan” sent to buffet him, and it does not say whether it was a bodily illness, an opponent or a trial of another kind. The passage does not say that the figure is literal or what its effect was. Different readings are held as possibilities only; the text does not choose among them.

title: What does “because of the angels” mean in 1 Corinthians 11:10?
summary: 1 Corinthians 11:10 says “For this cause ought the woman to have power on her head because of the angels”. The verse does not say which angels are meant, or why they bear on the matter, or what “power on her head” is.
text: KJV 1 Corinthians 11:10: “ought the woman to have power on her head because of the angels”. Greek New Testament (Tischendorf, eighth edition) 1 Corinthians 11:10: διὰ τοὺς ἀγγέλους [because of the angels]. KJV 1 Corinthians 11:5: “every woman that prayeth or prophesieth with her head uncovered dishonoureth her head”. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/46/11/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/46/11/.
reasoning: The verse gives a reason (“because of the angels”) and does not say who they are or how they relate to the covering. The Greek word ἄγγελοι can mean heavenly beings or human messengers, and the passage does not say which it takes. “Power on her head” is likewise not defined in the verse. Different readings are held as possibilities only; the text does not choose among them.
